newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish radical Islamist MP quits Erbakan party.
newsitem.headline: Turkish radical Islamist MP quits Erbakan party.

text.p: A radical Islamist MP resigned on Thursday from caretaker Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Welfare Party, Anatolian news agency said.
It said deputy Ibrahim Halil Celik had quit the party but gave no more details. Celik was facing party discipline for allegedly making radical Islamist statements.
Erbakan resigned on Wednesday in an attempt to hand over power to coalition partner Tansu Ciller and deflect army criticism from his Islamist-led government.

It was unclear whether Celik's resignation would affect the planned power transfer. Two other Welfare radical deputies left the party on Wednesday but they would be expected to follow Erbakan's lead in any confidence vote in a new government.
President Suleyman Demirel on Thursday began a series of meetings with opposition leaders to decide who he will name as prime minister-designate.
Ciller and main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz are the candidates most tipped to get the nod from the president.
